scenes.narration: You cannot remember what you said last Tuesday. But play one bar of a song from twenty years ago and every word comes back instantly.
Music lights up more of the brain than almost anything else. Rhythm, melody, emotion, movement and language all activate at the same time.
Because so many regions are involved, the memory gets written in multiple places at once. It is like saving one file to five different hard drives.
There is a second reason. Most of your strongest musical memories come from ages ten to twenty five, a period when the brain is aggressively forming identity.
So when an old song hits and you feel something you cannot explain, that is not nostalgia for the music. It is recognition of yourself.
